requirements.summary: chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers applied and confirmed via ls -laR immediately after the change and again as a final check; inventorysvc user existed as a newly created system account.
Directories set to 750 and files to 640 with group inventory-readers; a live sudo -u test as a group member (reader_test) successfully read the file content, directly demonstrating group readability.

A sudo -u test as an unrelated user (other_test) was denied both file read (Permission denied) and directory listing (Permission denied) after the 750/640 permissions were applied, directly demonstrating the deny behavior for non-members.

sha256sum of config.json and records.csv captured before ownership/permission changes matches the prepare-time baseline hashes and the post-change/post-restart hashes exactly, confirming byte-for-byte preservation.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id, uptime, checksums, permissions) captured, reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect, connection loss observed during reboot, reconnection with a differing boot_id confirmed, and post-restart state re-verified (checksums, ownership/permissions, user/group existence) all match pre-restart baseline. Cross-checked by the fixed global before/after-executor boot-identity observations, which show the same boot_id transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied with direct evidence: ownership was set to inventorysvc, group-based read access for inventory-readers and denial for unrelated users were both empirically demonstrated via live sudo -u tests (not just permission bits), and file contents were verified byte-identical via checksums before, immediately after, and post-restart. The mandatory node1 restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated, cross-checked against the fixed global lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Directory-listing denial for the unrelated user was demonstrated by attempting readdir (ls), which is sufficient evidence of directory-traversal restriction but the trace does not separately test bare traversal (cd) into a file whose name is already known.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor created two temporary test accounts (reader_test, other_test) solely to directly verify the access-control requirement via sudo -u; this is a bounded, low-risk mutation directly tied to demonstrating a material outcome (group readability vs. other-user denial). Removal initially failed because the accounts had active systemd --user sessions (cmd-ac5865ed6ddb45cc), but the executor promptly killed those sessions and force-removed the accounts (cmd-304fad56838c4829), leaving no residual users per the final getent check. The lifecycle diff confirms no unexpected package, service, or socket drift between after-prepare and after-executor beyond the expected boot-identity change and ephemeral systemd-private temp directories tied to the reboot itself. A small /tmp/reboot.log file was left behind as a byproduct of the backgrounded reboot command, a negligible and expected artifact of the restart protocol.
